chapter_seo_title: Dao Guai Yi Xian Ch. 562: Li Huowang Gets Zapped and Stabbed by a Lying Ghost
chapter_meta_description: The State Preceptor unleashes heavenly thunder against the Zuowandao Dice! But in the Dao-Twisted World, killing a liar is never that easy. Li Huowang fights a desperate battle against a mind-invading spirit.
og_description: Huangfu Tiangong wants to barbecue everyone. Li Huowang has to trust a man who wouldn't hesitate to kill him.
twitter_description: The Dice is cornered, but his final attack is a whisper of another name. Li Huowang must fight his own mind.

lore_anchors.definition: The highest-ranking Daoist or Buddhist advisor to the emperor, often wielding immense political and supernatural power. In this novel, Huangfu Tiangong is a state-sanctioned enforcer of cosmic order.

A powerful and orthodox Daoist ritual magic said to command the Five Celestial Emperors of Thunder. It is used for exorcism, punishing evil, and summoning storms. Here, it is a terrifyingly brutal tool of state power.

A high-ranking member of the Zuowandao. His power is not brute strength but the manipulation of narrative and expectations. He treats battles as a game of strategy, always thinking several moves ahead.
A sword name derived from Daoist astrology, implying a weapon that channels the power of constellations, the celestial "ladder" a perfected spirit climbs to heaven.

A heretical, pain-worshipping sect in the novel. Their techniques, like impaling oneself with a rib, trade unimaginable agony for a corresponding supernatural effect, representing the ultimate cost for power.

cultural_notes_faq.q: What is the “Thunder Magic” the State Preceptor uses?
cultural_notes_faq.a: It’s a real, high-level Daoist ritual technique (五雷法 / Five Thunder Magic) used to command celestial thunder for exorcism and judgment, not just a generic lightning spell.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why does Li Huowang stab himself?
cultural_notes_faq.a: To counter the Dice’s mental invasion. By causing himself extreme pain, he hopes to force the Dice’s consciousness (which is parasitic on his thoughts) to lose its grip or be disrupted.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Who is the mysterious archer at the end?
cultural_notes_faq.a: A hidden protector of the Great Liang palace, showing that the imperial court has powers beyond just the State Preceptor, a new variable in this conflict.
